. sensory mass – maynooth st mary’s parish, maynooth, warmly invites you to our sensory mass on the fourth saturday of each month at 5pm . this mass is designed to be inclusive and welcoming for young people and families who may benefit from a quieter and more relaxed worship environment. the short mass will have gentle lighting and sound, calm atmosphere, space to move around if needed and sensory items to aid regulation. please join us and invite anyone who might have sensory needs or simply wishes to attend a short and peaceful mass. join us in the pastoral centre after for refreshments. eircode w23 n663. vocations we are delighted to share some very encouraging news from the vocations team: there are now six people studying for the archdiocese of dublin in 2026 — four in maynooth, studying philosophy and theology, and two beginning their propaedeutic year in valladolid, spain. we give heartfelt thanks to their families, friends and, especially, to the parishes and communities who have supported and encouraged these young men throughout their journey of discernment and continue to accompany them as they prepare for priesthood. we ask all our parishes and communities to continue to pray for vocations to the priesthood and religious life, and if you know someone who may be considering a vocation, please encourage them to get in touch with the vocations team. fr seamus mcentee or fr bill o’shaughnessy would be delighted to meet with them, listen to their story and accompany them on their journey of discernment. you can contact us at

/ 01 5529448. parish partnership name throughout the diocese parishes are being called to come together in new forms. grouping, cluster, amalgamation of parishes are the way ahead for the diocese that is reduced in priests to service local areas. we are privileged that the parish of saggart, rathcoole, brittas and the parish of newcastle have been working together for many years. a shared parish pastoral council and finance committee has been in place for a number of years showing a shared interest and cooperation between the ‘four districts’. we have been invited to discern a common name that has a resonance throughout the area. one suggestion raised recently was “mo sacra” a saint from the 7th century who set up a monastery in what is currently saggart cemetery. st brigid’s well in rathcoole, st. finian’s well in newcastle are other names. have you any thoughts or suggestions on a name that could be used. le chéile on saturday, november 7th, le chéile, an lgbtqi+ recognition and integration grou p in kimmage manor, together with st teresa’s parish, donore avenue, is hosting a workshop led by frank de bernardo of new ways ministry. it will take place in kimmage manor parish hall, from 2pm to 5pm. frank will share information about the church’s attitudes to, and teachings about, sexual/ gender identity, and offer practical advice as to how catholic parishes can support the lgbtqi+ community. all are welcome to attend, with prior registration necessary. to register, send an email to
